newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU oilseeds prices will be ruled by Chicago soya.
newsitem.headline: EU oilseeds prices will be ruled by Chicago soya.

text.p: Rapeseed demand from Poland and sunflowerseed exports from Russia and Ukraine will be the swing factors in a European Union oilseeds market heavily led by Chicago soybean prices this year, brokers and analysts said.
A broadly steady domestic EU oilseeds crop would mean its protein markets would be dominated by the powerful US soybean price, which reflects 50 percent of global oilseed supply.
"The EU crop is well on course after successful plantings...local weather impact will be limited," said German oilseeds broker Juergen Kiefer.
"Prices could be lifted by heavy Polish import demand for rapeseed while downward pressure from Ukrainian sunseed exports seems limited so far after reports of lower sowings."

Analysts put the total EU oilseed crop at 12-13 million tonnes, little changed from 1996. But domestic fundamentals are easily overruled by the fact that the EU needs to import some 13-14 million tonnes of soybeans each season.
"EU rapeseed cannot lead a life of its own because its products substitute or make way for soya purely on the basis of price," explained Kiefer, an authorised Matif rapeseed broker.

World oilseeds prices look set to ease when forecasts of higher United States soybean crops materialise late this year. But EU rapeseed could take support from sales to Poland, where a severe winter damaged the crop.
The Warsaw farm ministry said a week ago rapeseed output may fall to 400,000-450,000 tonnes in 1997 from 500,000 tonnes in 1996 and would meet only 40 percent of domestic demand.
Analysts said import tariff rates would affect German sales and support levels for EU prices.
Plantings of Russian and Ukrainean sunseed, the other factor in the EU supply balance, were delayed amid cold and rainy weather last month but farmers may be able to catch up.
Last year, the EU imported 1.78 million tonnes of Russian and Ukrainean sunseed, 1.40 million more than in 1995, data from independent Oil World newsletter showed.
The unexpected supply influx was bearish for oilseeds prices in the EU and likely 1997 sales are hard to predict.
The EU's stable oilseeds crop will be a result of a higher acreage which will help offset yield reductions in French rapeseed and Spanish sunseed after early 1997 drought in Europe's south and west.
Dutch analyst Arie van Dijk of statisticians Stigevo put the EU's main oilseeds crop, rape, at 8.2 million tonnes in 1997, up one million from last year.
But he added feed industry demand for protein meals from domestic and imported seeds should be low because outbreaks of swine fever in the Netherlands had reduced pigfeed consumption.
Ample meal supplies should be augmented by a good field peas crop and increasing supplies of citruspulp and cornglutenfeed via the Rotterdam import markets.
"It will be a buyers' market," van Dijk said.
Kiefer said oil markets were less well supplied because EU food industries needed to stock up on vegetable oils.

Imported Latin American soybeans in Europe last cost just under $340 a tonne for the summer months, while new crop U.S. beans for Oct-Jan are priced in the high $280s. North European rapeseed buyers free Hamburg were at 487.50 marks/t for June last Friday, with August new crop at 452.50.
